Question:
If \(p\) and \(q\) are primes and \(x^2-px+q=0\) has distinct positive integral roots, then which of the following statements are true?

I. The difference of the roots is odd.

II. At least one root is prime.

III. \(p^2-q\) is prime.

IV. \(p+q\) is prime.
